title: Doing life together Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’My command is this: Love each other as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends. You are my friends if you do what I command. I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know his master’s business. Instead, I have called you friends, for everything that I learned from my Father I have made known to you. You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you so that you might go and bear fruit—fruit that will last—and so that whatever you ask in my name the Father will give you This is my command: Love each other.’’
devotional:
Friendships are such an essential part of life, and loneliness can be a threat to life. Jesus had a lot of important things to say about friendship. The text we are looking at is part of Jesus’ final words to his disciples on the night before he died. We need to keep that in mind, for the context of these words give them a greater seriousness. Jesus is preparing his disciples for the future, He is giving them essential instructions so they can live the life he wants them to live.

There are a number of lessons we can learn from what Jesus says in these verses.

Relationships are more important than programmes.

If you look carefully at these verses they start and end the same way. ‘This is my command that you love each other.’ John 15:12, 17. When you think about it, this on the surface appears to be a strange thing to say. If you were leaving your work in the hands of someone else, you might give them a strategy, or a ‘to do list,’ or some kind of programme to follow. But Jesus does not do that. He simply commands that we love each other.

Sometimes in church life we find it easier to invest in programmes than in relationships. Programmes are always dispensable, relationships are never. The love that Christians should have for each other is the only foundation for authentic evangelism. In John 13:34-35 Jesus said ‘A new commandment I give you. Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. By this all men will know that that you are my disciples, if you love one another.’

Generally do you think churches pray more about programmes than they do about relationships? Are we inclined to operate as if programmes are more important than relationships?

Friendship is the natural, spontaneous outworking of the love of God in someone’s life. ‘Friend’ was the word Jesus used to describe the natural consequence of his love for his disciples. What does it mean to Love one another as friends? The word the bible often uses for love is AGAPE.

What is AGAPE love?

The source of agape love is not the character of the person who is being loved, or even their need, but rather it is about the character and nature of the person who is ‘doing the loving.’

The quality of agape love is unconditional, it is not based on merit, and it does not need to be deserved.

The goal of agape love is always the highest good of the other person, no matter the cost.

The evidence of agape love is action. It is not emotion centred but will centred. It is practical, it chooses to act.

The extent of agape love is sacrificial. The true nature of love will always lead to sacrifice.

To be a friend means that we need to receive God’s love for us. When we read the words ‘Love each other as I have loved you,’ it would very easy to feel overwhelmed with such a request, and in being overwhelmed we are inclined to draw back and think that Jesus is making an unreasonable demand. The key to loving others is God’s love for us. As we receive, embrace and enjoy God’s love for us, we will be secure enough to love others. Sometimes others are badly affected and suffer greatly when we refuse to receive God’s love for us.
prayer: Father forgive us when we live and act in a way that says programmes are more important than relationships.
